title: defining `process` as `true` breaks usage of libraries looking for environment variables
body:
**Describe the bug**

[`process` is defined as `true` using the webpack define plugin](https://github.com/storybooks/storybook/blob/6adbf6b4c605b3628acb73293ae9fe1889404d2a/lib/core/src/server/manager/manager-webpack.config.js#L63). `true` does not match the expectation that `process` is an object. 

this results in libraries, even when attempting to be defensive about the presence of `process`, attempting to perform object actions against a boolean and therefore throwing errors at runtime.

the specific example that is giving me trouble is with the [browser version](https://github.com/visionmedia/debug/blob/5c7c61dc0df0db4eb5de25707d8cd1b9be1add4f/src/browser.js#L216) of [`debug`](https://github.com/visionmedia/debug).

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. import `debug` into one of your stories
2. navigate to that story within storybook
3. See error in the browser console

**Expected behavior**

process should either be left as undefined and expected to be added by projects that need it or at least defined using a shape that matches the expected contract. please also see [this comment](https://github.com/visionmedia/debug/issues/467#issuecomment-448419976) from a maintainer of debug about the contract of `process`

**error**

<details>
<summary>the error thrown in the case of `debug`</summary>

```
TypeError: Cannot use 'in' operator to search for 'env' in true
    at Function.load (browser.js?34eb:221)
    at setup (common.js?dc90:261)
    at eval (browser.js?34eb:250)
    at Object../node_modules/debug/src/browser.js (vendors~main.90358a9d4fdec3ed3967.bundle.js:75360)
    at __webpack_require__ (runtime~main.90358a9d4fdec3ed3967.bundle.js:782)
    at fn (runtime~main.90358a9d4fdec3ed3967.bundle.js:150)
    at eval (any.es.js?d9f8:39)
    at Module../node_modules/@travi/any/lib/any.es.js (vendors~main.90358a9d4fdec3ed3967.bundle.js:68352)
    at __webpack_require__ (runtime~main.90358a9d4fdec3ed3967.bundle.js:782)
    at fn (runtime~main.90358a9d4fdec3ed3967.bundle.js:150)
```

</details>

**Code snippets**

https://github.com/visionmedia/debug/blob/5c7c61dc0df0db4eb5de25707d8cd1b9be1add4f/src/browser.js#L216

**System:**
 - OS: MacOS
 - Device: Macbook Pro 2016
 - Browser: chrome
 - Framework: react
 - Addons: actions, info, links
 - Version: [e.g. 4.0.0] found initially on `v5.1.0-alpha.40`, but have confirmed that it still exists in `v5.1.0-beta.0`

**Additional context**

i did add [a comment](https://github.com/storybooks/storybook/pull/6553/files#r282690991) yesterday evening against the commit that appeared to add this definition. its it can be bad form to comment against closed issues, i figured a more formal issue could be better. please don't see the double filing as any additional pressure from me. i'm just trying to follow up to get you the info that aligns with your normal process.
